supported_claims.text: The conventional analysis treats 假 as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 contributes a person-related meaning and 叚 supplies a sound cue. This analysis is recorded in the Shuowen account and other compiled analyses; the evidence does not establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.

A scholarly proposal instead treats 人 as a semantic addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing. It reports 叚 in pre-Qin excavated texts and 假 in Qin-period documents, and reads a dated Qin example as distinguishing lending from borrowing; this interpretation is not settled and was not checked against a manuscript facsimile in this research.

The cited evidence records both borrowing and false or untrue uses of 假, but it does not securely establish which sense came first or a continuous semantic path between them. A classical borrowing example and a separate false/not-so example are reported, without secure first-attestation dating.

Evidence about 叚 describes it as an older graph with uses read as blessing, fault, interrogative words and other forms, as well as the gloss “borrow.” These are reported readings and uses of 叚, not a demonstrated semantic chronology for 假.

disagreements.text: The conventional account analyzes 亻 as semantic and 叚 as phonetic, while the Qin-text proposal treats 人 as a graphic differentiator associated with distinguishing uses of the word. The dossier does not resolve these accounts.

A proposed development from “borrow” through “simulate” to “false” is not established by the cited attestations. The competing proposal argues for graphic differentiation and disputes deriving “false” from “borrow.”

limitations.text: No suitable ancient glyph image for 假 was verified or visually inspected, and a detailed sequence of dated graphic changes was not established. The description of bronze forms for 叚 is a reported analysis, not an independently inspected image.

The reported Old Chinese comparisons place 假 and 叚 together in some reconstruction data, but the dossier provides no independently verified character-specific pronunciation record and does not establish the historical phonetic role solely from the modern readings. Different reconstruction systems must remain distinct.

The Qin-period distinction between 叚 and 假, including the lending-versus-borrowing interpretation, is reported by a scholarly article; no manuscript facsimile was independently inspected, and later usage is reported to mix the forms.
